key_insight: VQE can be substantially manipulated by adversarial attacks in cloud-style workflows, with noise-induced attacks that exploit the Zero-Noise Extrapolation pipeline causing the largest energy-error amplification.
engineering_relevance: For quantum chemistry and materials workflows, VQE results should be treated as security-sensitive outputs and defended with benchmarking, monitoring, and pipeline hardening across the full transpilation-to-execution stack.
method: Built VQE-AdvBench, a unified red-teaming benchmark for adversarial robustness of VQE.
Organized attacks by black-, gray-, and white-box access to compare threats under one protocol.
Evaluated seven attack scenarios across H2 and H3+ on five noise-calibrated IBM backends using a fixed molecule-ansatz-backend-metric setup.
evidence_signal: Across the benchmark, noise-induced QNBAD variants were most damaging with up to 8.84× error amplification, followed by QTrojan at 7.52×, while QDoor reached only 1.37×.
watch_item: Results are benchmark-specific and depend on the chosen molecules, ansatz, backends, and noise calibration, so broader generalization to other VQE settings still needs validation.
paper_title: SoK: Adversarial Robustness of the Variational Quantum Eigensolver via Red-Teaming
